solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Travelling US area, Turk delivers cabbage dish

indicators.note: things travelling move about, so these letters are on the move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Turkish traveller in America hands out a cabbage dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' shuffles US, AREA and TURK together; 'delivers' only links fodder to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauerkraut is finely cut fermented cabbage, a German speciality served as a side.

clue.text: Gelatinous substance produced by a fish more than once

indicators.note: doing something more than once here means the piece appears twice in a row

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish (garfish)

explanation.surface: A jelly-like stuff is made by some fish, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus GAR, then 'more than once' repeats the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a jelly extracted from seaweed, used as a gelling agent in labs and cooking.

clue.text: Journalist covering current Muslim festival

indicators.note: the outer piece wraps around and so covers the inner one

parts.note: ED, an editor, is the crossword's stock journalist
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A reporter is covering this year's Muslim festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as 'present-day' but is the physics symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: Eid is the name of either of two major Islamic feasts, al-Fitr and al-Adha.

clue.text: Noted canonical hour, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: none (or nones) is the monastic office said at the ninth hour, pronounced to rhyme with 'bone'

explanation.surface: A recognised time of church prayer, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The office NONE is said 'nohn', which matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone noted is well recognised or famous, the adjective sense.

clue.text: Nob accommodating old Italian poet

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a nob is a toff, informally an aristo(crat)

explanation.surface: A posh person puts up an elderly Italian versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: ARISTO takes O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludovico Ariosto wrote the Renaissance epic Orlando Furioso.

clue.text: Dog's plaything originally designed in SW resort

parts.note: a toy is a plaything

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the resort's name

parts.note: Poole is a seaside town in Dorset, south-west England

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A dog's toy was first designed in a south-western seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's' is 'Dog is'. POOLE is a resort town in Dorset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy poodle is the smallest variety of poodle breed.

clue.text: Unqualified character on the staff

definitions.meaning: a musical sign written on the stave

explanation.surface: An unskilled member of the employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests workers; it is the musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means outright or absolute, and is also the music symbol lowering a note a semitone.

clue.text: Promotion of article supporting ancient city in EU country

indicators.note: the city and article are placed inside the country's name

parts.note: France is a member of the European Union

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: Advocacy of a grammatical article backing an old city somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts the article beneath the city; 'Promotion' means advancement, not a sales push.
explanation.definitionFit: Furtherance is the advancement or forwarding of a cause, which is what promotion does.

clue.text: Obscure place to shop, having note for daughter

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, the swap 'for' signals

parts.note: an arcade is a covered walkway of shops
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
N is the abbreviation for note (as in banknotes)

explanation.surface: A little-known shopping centre has had its musical note taken from a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCADE swaps its D for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane knowledge is secret or mysterious, understood by few.

clue.text: Time one secures a new opening for Indian cooking

indicators.note: the numeral gets hold of the pieces and so comes after them in sequence

parts.note: a door is an opening into a room
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Time for someone to get a fresh opening in curry-making.
explanation.walkthrough: T, A, N and DOOR, with I at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori food is roasted in a clay oven, a style of Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Jester initially impressing court in northern city

indicators.note: those letters go inside the city's name

parts.note: York is a city in northern England

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A clown is first winning over royal court in a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' serves both 'impressing' and 'court'; York is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorick is the dead court fool whose skull Hamlet holds up.

clue.text: Fish served by maid primarily in reception room

indicators.note: the letter is set within the room

parts.note: a salon is a drawing or reception room

indicators.note: primarily, meaning first of all, picks the opening letter

explanation.surface: A fish is served by the maid in the drawing room.
explanation.walkthrough: M put within SALON.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmon is a well-known game and food fish.

clue.text: Novel 1,760-yard hike consuming a couple of days

indicators.note: eating up, so the outer word takes the other in

parts.note: a mile is 1,760 yards
D for day, twice
a march is a long walk

explanation.surface: A long walk lasts a mile and eats up two days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is the definition, a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlemarch is George Eliot's celebrated Victorian novel of provincial life.

clue.text: Calming report of woman with phobia

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the letters are taken from the sound

parts.note: SUE is a woman's name, and a 'thing' is an irrational fear (to have a thing about spiders)

explanation.surface: A soothing account of a woman who is afraid of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'Sue thing' matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Soothing things relax or calm a person.

clue.text: Light-bearer's container held back by former queen

parts.note: a can is a container

indicators.note: back means the word held is read in reverse

parts.note: old means former
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A lamp's casing was kept back by a past monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held back' is fodder and indicator: DLEH. 'Light-bearer's' is 'Light-bearer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A candleholder holds a candle, so it bears the light.

clue.text: Suitable former exercise regime any number accepted

parts.note: ex means former
PE is physical education

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so N goes inside

parts.note: a diet is a regime of eating
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: An old fitness plan that has taken any number of people is suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is British school sport; N as 'any number' comes from algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means convenient or advantageous for the purpose, so suitable.

clue.text: Russian empress in dire straits over article

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the other
being in a dire state suggests the letters are in a mess

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Russian empress is in deep trouble over some item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In dire straits' looks like the idiom; 'in dire' shuffles STRAITS to TSARITS, then A below.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsaritsa is a tsar's wife or a woman ruler of Russia.

clue.text: Cuts fish by loch, adopting duke's crooked posture

parts.note: lops means cuts off

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the duke goes inside

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
Loch Ness, the Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a fish beside a Scottish lake while the duke stands bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adopting' acts on fish and loch together; 'duke's' is 'duke has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopsidedness is being uneven or tilted, so a crooked stance.

clue.text: Popular girl to west of Ohio?

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
Diana is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A well-liked young woman heads west past Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by location.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is the US state directly bordering Ohio on its western side.

clue.text: In Columbus he lacked a measure of corn

indicators.note: In says the answer is found inside the next words

explanation.surface: In Columbus, Ohio, a man was short of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'ColumBUS HE Lacked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushel is a dry measure of volume used for grain.

clue.text: Old hat banned by doctor penning poem

parts.note: out, as in ruled out or prohibited

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the doctor surrounds the poem

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: An old hat was banned by a doctor who writes verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like headgear; it means passé.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for dated or no longer fashionable.

clue.text: Rocky island in southern Irish county

parts.note: Kerry is a county in south-west Ireland

explanation.surface: A rocky island sits in a southern Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a small rocky reef or isle, a word from Scottish waters.

clue.text: Rose's part in Sophocles's Antigone finally overcoming friend

indicators.note: in a down clue, to be over something is to sit above it
finally applies to each word, taking its last letter

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A rose figures in a Greek tragedy, finally getting the better of a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: S and E, the ends of the two names, above PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like parts enclosing a flower bud, roses included.

clue.text: Hamlet's odd theory mostly about Polonius's entrance?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes around the letter
odd suggests these letters are strangely arranged
mostly means all but the last letter
an entrance is the way in, so the first letter

explanation.surface: A strange idea about Polonius coming on stage in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: THEOR shuffled to THORE round P. 'Hamlet's' is 'Hamlet is': not the play but a village.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorpe is an old word for a hamlet or village, common in English place names.

clue.text: Old man from the east with little desire for food?

indicators.note: in an across clue, going from the east means right to left

parts.note: pa is father, one's old man
petite means small

explanation.surface: A father coming from the east with a tiny appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: PA read backwards gives AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is the natural wish to eat.

clue.text: Expedition missing out top of Umbrian peak

indicators.note: missing out means leaving a letter behind

parts.note: a tour is a journey or expedition

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trip skipping the summit of an Italian mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUR loses U.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hilltop, the summit of a hill on Dartmoor.

clue.text: Contemptuous cry about Liberal claptrap

indicators.note: about means around, so the cry surrounds the letter

parts.note: bah is an exclamation of contempt

explanation.surface: A scornful shout about the Liberals' nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: BAH with L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah is empty or pretentious talk, which claptrap is.

clue.text: Fisher's alarm went off at sea around east of Humber

indicators.note: around means the anagram surrounds the letter
gone off and at sea both suggest confusion, so these letters are mixed up
in an across word, the east end is the last letter

explanation.surface: A fisherman's alarm sounded at sea near the Humber estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: ALARMWENT shuffled round R, the last letter of Humber, an English river estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: A trawlerman works on a trawler, a fishing vessel.
